title: Isolation of macrophages from mouse skin wounds for single-cell RNA sequencing
protocol: Anesthetize a mouse by intraperitoneal injection of Ketavet and Xylazin in sterile 0.9% NaCl solution.
Cover the eyes of the mouse with eye ointment.
Shave the back skin of the mouse with an electric shaver for animals.
Disinfect the back skin with a paper towel soaked in 70% ethanol.
Perform 4 full thickness punch injuries in the back skin left and right of the spine using a biopsy puncher (4 mm in diameter).
Keep the mouse on a heating plate at 37°C in a laminar flow hood until it wakes up.
Place the mouse into a clean autoclaved cage which should contain autoclaved tissue instead of beddings after waking up.
Exchange the autoclaved tissues daily up to day 3 after injury.
Keep the wounded mouse separated from other mice until the wound tissue is excised.
Add 1 mg/mL tramadol to the drinking water up to day 3 after injury.
Sacrifice the mice according to institutional guidelines.
Excise the wound tissues with forceps and scissors.
Place the wound tissue onto a wooden spatula.
Remove the skin surrounding the wound tissue, leaving 0.5–1.0 mm of normal skin around the wound.
Cut the wound tissue into small pieces (∼ 1 mm edge length).
Transfer the cut wound tissue into a 1.5 mL tube filled with 1.2 mL of DMEM medium.
Add 30 μg/mL Liberase TM Research Grade to the DMEM medium for enzymatic digestion.
Incubate the wound tissue in the digestion medium for 1 h at 37°C in a ThermoMixer (shaking at 400/min).
Mix the wound tissue manually every 15 min by taking the tube out of the ThermoMixer and shaking it.
Transfer the digested wound tissue into a Medicon after incubation.
Homogenize the wound tissue for 5 min in the Medicon.
Aspirate the single-cell suspension with a 1 mL syringe.
Aspirate the digested wound tissue together with the digestion medium using a 1 mL pipette tip.
Transfer the aspirated mixture into a Medicon.
Close the lid of the Medicon and homogenize the tissue mechanically for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the wound cell suspension with a 1 mL syringe.
Pour the cell suspension through a 70 μM cell strainer into a 50 mL tube on ice.
Rinse the Medicon with 2 mL DMEM.
Pour the rinse through the 70 μM cell strainer into the 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 8 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 2 mL of FB1.
Aspirate the wound cell suspension and pour it through a 40 μM cell strainer into a 50 mL tube.
Rinse the 40 μM cell strainer with 3 mL of FB1.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 8 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant carefully.
Add 1 mL of Red Blood Cell Lysis Solution to the cell pellet.
Incubate at 18°C–25°C for 2 minutes.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 8 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 μL of FB1.
Transfer cell suspension into a 96 well conical (V) bottom plate for FACS staining.
Centrifuge 96-well plate at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant and discard it.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 100 μL of FB2 with anti-CD16/CD32 and incubate for 10 min at 4°C.
Centrifuge 96-well plate at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant and discard it.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 100 μL of antibody mix and incubate for 20 min at 4°C in the dark.
Centrifuge 96-well plate at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant and discard it.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 μL of FB2.
Centrifuge 96-well plate at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant and discard it.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 μL of FB2.
Centrifuge 96-well plate at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant and discard it.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 100 μL of FB2.
Add 50 ng/mL DAPI to the resuspended cells.
Pour the cell suspension through a 40 μm cell strainer into a FACS tube.
Keep the sample tubes on ice and in the dark.
Activate appropriate laser lines on the flow cytometer.
Ensure filters and mirrors match fluorochromes used.
Set up PMT voltages and perform compensation using single stain controls.
Minimize fluorochrome spill-over to avoid high compensation.
Determine appropriate compensation for each fluorescence parameter.
Use FMO controls to assess autofluorescence for each fluorescence parameter.
Install a 100 μm nozzle on the flow cytometer.
Bring the ACDU to the front of the instrument.
Optimize drop delay according to BD FACS Diva reference manual instructions.
Install a collection plate preloaded with 0.5 μL of Lysis Buffer per well.
Choose the appropriate device layout for sample deposition.
Switch on plate voltage.
Activate "test sort".
Optimize far left side stream to pass through splash shield with minimal deflection.
Bring ACDU to home position.
Deposit drop by shortly activating “test sort” button.
Inspect deposition of the drop.
Adjust home position to hit the center of well A1.
Sort single polystyrene beads premixed in PBS with horse radish peroxidase solution (100 μg/mL) into individual wells containing 1 μL of 3,3′,5,5′-Tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) solution.
Set sort precision “single cell”.
Target event = 1.
Choose as target cell population gate DAPI- single CD45+CD11b+F4/80+ macrophages.
Backgate CD45+CD11b+F4/80+ cells before starting sorting.
Check the "Index Sorting" option for additional markers such as MHC II, Trem2, CD301b, Ly6C, CCR2, and CD64 to identify macrophages.
Use lineage markers like CD3ε, NK1.1, B220, Siglec F, and Ly6G to exclude non-macrophage cell populations.
Ensure appropriate gating thresholds using Fluorescence Minus One (FMO) controls for dimly positive populations.
Sort single macrophages using index sorting.
Record a data file containing all events from each sort run.
Create an index sort file with well ID and optical parameters of sorted events.
Minimize sorting/processing time to less than 30 minutes to one hour.
Perform a pre-adjustment trial run on the FACS sorter to establish settings.
Optimize the sorting stream as suggested in step 53 of the colorimetric assay before sorting begins.
Use cell strainers to remove aggregates during steps 21 and 26.
Liberate red blood cells according to step 30 instructions.
Adjust the cell suspension density to approximately 5 × 10^6/mL.
Seal the sorting plate as long as possible to prevent evaporation of Lysis Buffer.
Uncover the sorting plate immediately before beginning the sort process.
Seal plates with adhesive foil after sorting is complete.
Centrifuge sorted plates at a minimum of 100 × g for one minute at 4°C to collect liquid at the bottom.
Freeze the plates at -80°C for at least one hour or up to four months.
Thaw the plates on ice.
Add 0.5 μL of dT-Buffer to each well of the 384-well plate using a nanodispenser.
Heat-seal the plate for 1 second at 166°C.
Mix the contents thoroughly.
Spin down the plate to pellet any bubbles or debris.
Incubate the plate for 3 min at 72°C to denature RNA.
Prepare the Reverse Transcription Buffer on ice as described in the materials and equipment section.
Add 1.5 μL of the prepared buffer to each well of the 384-well plate using a nanodispenser.
Heat-seal the plate (1 s at 166°C) and spin it down.
Vortex thoroughly and spin it down once more.
Perform Reverse Transcription as per protocol instructions.
Prepare cDNA Amplification Master Mix as described.
Add 3 μL of the cDNA Amplification Master Mix to each well using a nanodispenser.
Heat-seal the plate for 1 second at 166°C.
Vortex the plate and spin it down.
Amplify cDNA with cycling conditions specified in the protocol.
Keep amplified cDNA at 4°C for up to 8–16 hours or at −20°C for a few days.
Purify amplified cDNA using magnetic bead purification on a liquid handling robot.
Add 9 μL of magnetic beads to each well and mix well.
Incubate the mixture for 5 minutes at 18°C–25°C.
Place the mixture on the magnet for 3 minutes.
Wash beads twice with 30 μL of 80% ethanol.
Dry bead pellet by vacuum centrifuge for 8 minutes at 30°C if necessary to remove remaining ethanol.
Elute beads in 12 μL nuclease-free water.
Allow beads and cDNA to rehydrate at 18°C–25°C for approximately 1 hour.
Store samples at 4°C for up to 16 hours or at -20°C for up to 6 months.
Analyze fragment size distribution and measure concentration of the cDNA using a fragment analyzer for randomly picked samples.
Load 20 μL of AccuBlue BR dsDNA Quantitation Mix into each well of a 384-well black LV plate.
Add 1.5 μL of purified cDNA to each well containing the AccuBlue BR dsDNA Quantitation Mix.
Prepare a standard row with at least eight measure points covering the concentration range of the samples in triplicates: 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1, 0.5, and 0 ng/μL of standard.
Measure the concentration of all samples using appropriate excitation and emission parameters.
Transfer 2 μL (700 pg) of the amplified cDNA in an empty 384-well plate.
Desiccate the liquid completely by vacuum centrifuge for 15 min at 30°C.
Thaw all reagents from the Tagmentation Master Mix A on ice.
Prepare the Tagmentation Master Mix A according to the materials and equipment section instructions.
Add 1 μL of Tagmentation Master Mix A with a nanodispenser to each well.
Heat-seal the plate for 1 s at 166°C.
Vortex vigorously and spin down the plate.
Incubate the plate in a pre-heated thermal cycler using the specified program.
Add 3 μL of KAPA High-Fidelity Hot Start ReadyMix (2×) to each well.
Add 2 μL of P5 and P7 barcoded Nextera amplification primers (1 μM of each) per well, making a total reaction volume of 6 μL.
Heat-seal the plate.
Vortex and spin down the plate.
Amplify tagmented DNA with the specified cycling conditions.
Add 10 μL of nuclease-free water to each sample to reach a total volume of 16 μL.
Heat-seal the plate at 166°C for 1 s, vortex thoroughly and spin it down.
Transfer 3 µL of cDNA to an empty 384-well plate.
Desiccate the liquid completely by vacuum centrifuge for 15 - 20 min at 30°C.
Add 1 μL of Tagmentation Master Mix B with a nanodispenser to each well and heat-seal the plate for 1 sec at 166°C.
Vortex the plate vigorously and spin it down for a total of 3 times, but stop last spin at 45 x g.
Incubate the plate in a thermal cycler for 15 min at 55°C (without pre-heated lid).
Add 1 μL of 0.1% SDS to each sample to stop the reaction.
Heat-seal the lid again, mix well and incubate for 15 min at 37°C.
Quickly spin the plate down and place it on a 384-well magnetic rack to separate the beads from the supernatant.
Fully remove the supernatant.
Add 2.5 µL of KAPA High-Fidelity Hot Start Ready Mix to each sample.
Add 2.5 µL of nuclease-free water to each sample.
Add 100 nL of P5 and 100 nL of P7 Nextera index primers using a nanodispenser.
Heat-seal the plate, vortex and spin it down.
Pre-heat lid to 105°C for amplification cycling conditions.
Add 8 µL of nuclease-free water to each sample to reach a total volume of 13 µL.
Transfer 12 µL to a new plate suitable for liquid handling automated systems if necessary.
Seal the plate, mix and spin it down.
Load 20 μL of AccuBlue BR dsDNA Quantitation Mix into each well of a 384-well black LV plate.
Add 1.5 μL of unpurified library to each well for quantification.
Prepare a standard row covering the concentration range of libraries in triplicates (covering concentrations: 80, 60, 40, 20, 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1, 0.5 and a blank value).
Seal the plate with foil.
Vortex and spin down the plate.
Incubate for at least 10 minutes at 18°C–25°C in the dark.
Remove foil before measurement.
Spin down the plate quickly.
Measure with a plate reader using appropriate excitation and emission parameters.
Evaluate library concentration according to values measured in the standard row.
Pool libraries equimolarly based on reader measurements and desired sequencing output.
Add 0.9× of Agencourt XP beads (or comparable) to each pool and mix well by pipetting up and down.
Incubate at 18°C–25°C for 5 minutes after mixing the beads with the pools.
Place tubes on a magnetic rack, discard supernatant once beads attach to the magnet.
Wash library pools twice with 200 μL of freshly-prepared 80% EtOH.
Wait 30 seconds between each wash before removing the EtOH.
Pulse-spin the tubes after washing and remove any residual EtOH.
Air-dry the beads at 18°C–25°C for approximately 5 minutes.
Hydrate magnetic beads with nuclease-free water for size selection.
Add 0.6× volume of hydrated magnetic beads to each library pool and incubate at 18°C–25°C for 5 minutes.
Place tubes on the magnetic rack to separate beads from buffer, then transfer supernatants into a new tube.
Add 0.9× of magnetic beads to each library pool and incubate at 18°C–25°C for 5 minutes.
Separate beads from buffer using the magnetic rack and discard all supernatant.
Keep tubes on magnetic rack and wash library pools twice with 200 μL of freshly-prepared 80% EtOH.
Wait for 30 s before removing the EtOH after each wash.
Pulse-spin the tubes, place them back in the magnetic rack and remove any residual EtOH.
Air-dry the beads at 18°C–25°C for approximately 2 min until they have a rusty color.
Dissolve the dried beads with appropriate volume of nuclease-free water.
Transfer all supernatant to a clean PCR tube after clearing solution by placing tubes on magnetic rack.
Analyze library size distribution and concentration using a fragment analyzer.
